Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.
